newsitem.title: USA: Figgie founder grants stk option to suitor.
newsitem.headline: Figgie founder grants stk option to suitor.

text.p: Harry Figgie Jr, founder of Figgie International Inc, has granted Heico Cos LLC an option to buy 235,647 class B common shares of the company, the shareholder said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday.
Figgie granted the option, equivalent of a 5.0 percent of the class B shares outstanding, a day after Chicago-based Heico renewed an offer to acquire the company at $15 a share.
Figgie International, a Willoughby, Ohio-based diversified manufacturer, had not responded to Heico's offer, according to the filing.

Heico's offer values Figgie International at about $276 million, based on 4.7 million class B shares and 13.7 million shares outstanding, according to Joel Reed, an official of Batchelder & Partners, financial advisers to the Figgie family.
The class B shares rose 1-1/2 to 14-1/4 on Thursday.
Figgie and his family, which hold a stake of about 19 percent in the manufacturer, has been pressing the company to spin off its units to shareholders without delay.
Figgie said the option to Heico includes the grant of a proxy to vote the shares in any formal merger proposal by Heico.

In return, Figgie agreed to refrain from negotiating with other parties to sell the 235,637 shares covered by the option or any other shares in the company that he owns. Figgie is allowed under the agreement to sell the shares in open market transactions.
An official of Figgie International was not immediately available to comment.
